usage: Standard pharmacy request; add 진통제 한 통 for a whole box
Use 먹다 for oral meds, not 마시다
센 (strong) is the natural everyday word here, not 강한
효과 있어요 = it works / is effective
examples: 머리가 너무 아픈데 진통제 있어요?
My head hurts so much, do you have any painkillers?
Common opener at a 약국 (pharmacy)
진통제 먹었는데도 안 나아요.
Even though I took a painkiller, it's not getting better.
-는데도 = even though; 안 나아요 = doesn't get better
생리통 때문에 진통제 두 알 먹었어요.
I took two painkillers because of menstrual cramps.
알 is the counter for pills/tablets
nuance: 진통제 is the everyday word for any pain-relief pill (headache, cramps, muscle pain) and pharmacists use it freely. In casual speech people often just name the brand, like 타이레놀, but 진통제 is the safe generic term. Tone is neutral and works in any register.
mistakes: Saying 진통제 마셔요 — pills are 먹다, not 마시다 (drink)
Confusing it with 해열제 (fever reducer); 진통제 targets pain, though some products do both

usage: Please give me some digestive medicine
Both pill and liquid types exist; 먹다 covers both colloquially
I bought digestive medicine because I couldn't digest
소화가 안 되다 = to have indigestion
a digestive medicine like Gas Hwalmyeongsu
Names a famous liquid 소화제 brand
examples: 체했는데 소화제 좀 주세요.
I have an upset stomach, please give me some digestive medicine.
체하다 = to have indigestion / stomach blocked, very common complaint
과식해서 소화제 먹고 누웠어요.
I overate so I took digestive medicine and lay down.
과식하다 = to overeat
소화제는 식후에 드세요.
Take the digestive medicine after meals.
식후 = after a meal; pharmacist instruction
nuance: 소화제 is what you ask for after eating too much or when you feel 체했어요 (stomach blocked). It covers both chewable tablets and the popular liquid bottles like 까스활명수. The word is neutral and used by everyone from teens to grandparents.
mistakes: Mixing it up with 위장약 — 소화제 is specifically for digestion/indigestion, 위장약 is broader (gastritis, acid)
Saying 소화약 — the correct word is 소화제 (the -제 suffix)

usage: Please give me a fever reducer
to give a fever reducer (to someone)
먹이다 = to feed/give meds, e.g. to a child
I had a fever so I took a fever reducer
열이 나다 = to run a fever
-용 = for the use of; ask this for kids
examples: 열이 38도가 넘어서 해열제 먹었어요.
My fever was over 38 degrees so I took a fever reducer.
Koreans cite 도 (degrees Celsius) for fever
해열제 먹어도 열이 안 떨어져요.
Even after taking a fever reducer, the fever won't come down.
열이 떨어지다 = the fever goes down
아이한테 해열제 먹이고 병원에 갔어요.
I gave my child a fever reducer and went to the hospital.
-한테 먹이다 = give medicine to someone
nuance: 해열제 is the go-to word when 열이 나요 (you have a fever); pharmacists immediately understand it. Many products combine 해열 and 진통 effects, so a pharmacist may hand you one pill for both. Neutral register, used in homes and clinics alike.
mistakes: Confusing 해열제 (lowers fever) with 감기약 (general cold medicine) — they overlap but aren't identical
Saying 열약 — the correct term is 해열제

usage: Please give me some cold medicine
Most common request when you catch a cold
먹다 for both pills and liquid sachets
Pharmacists ask 졸린 거 vs 안 졸린 거 (drowsy vs non-drowsy)
examples: 감기 기운이 있어서 감기약 사러 왔어요.
I'm coming down with a cold so I came to buy cold medicine.
감기 기운 = the onset/feeling of a cold, very natural phrase
안 졸린 감기약으로 주세요.
Please give me the non-drowsy cold medicine.
Crucial if you have to work/drive
감기약 먹고 푹 쉬었더니 좀 나아졌어요.
I took cold medicine and rested well, so I feel a bit better.
푹 쉬다 = to rest well; -았더니 shows result
nuance: 감기약 is the umbrella term for cold remedies and the single most common thing newcomers buy at a 약국. Pharmacists will ask about your main symptom (콧물, 기침, 목) and whether you want 졸린/안 졸린 (drowsy or not). Completely neutral and essential daily vocabulary.
mistakes: Asking only for 약 (medicine) — say 감기약 so the pharmacist knows what you need
Forgetting to mention symptoms; 감기약 varies a lot by 콧물/기침/열

usage: 바르다 is the correct verb for creams/ointments
I put ointment on the wound
Use the particle 에 for the spot
Specify the area: 피부(skin), 눈(eye → 안연고)
examples: 넘어져서 무릎에 연고 바르고 반창고 붙였어요.
I fell and put ointment on my knee and stuck on a band-aid.
Natural pairing of 연고 + 반창고
이 연고는 하루에 세 번 바르세요.
Apply this ointment three times a day.
하루에 세 번 = three times a day, standard dosage phrasing
벌레 물린 데 바르는 연고 있어요?
Do you have ointment for insect bites?
물린 데 = the bitten spot; 데 = place/spot
nuance: 연고 covers any medicated cream or ointment for skin (cuts, burns, bug bites, rashes), and the verb is always 바르다, never 먹다. If you need it for a specific spot, name it: 무좀 연고 (athlete's foot), 안연고 (eye ointment). Neutral, everyday register.
mistakes: Saying 연고 먹다 — ointment is applied (바르다), never eaten
Using 칠하다 (paint) instead of 바르다 for putting it on skin

usage: Please give me a pain patch
to stick on a pain patch
붙이다 is the verb for patches/stickers
I put a patch on my shoulder
Particle 에 marks the body part
뿌리다 = to spray; the spray type
examples: 어깨가 결려서 파스 붙였어요.
My shoulder is stiff so I put on a pain patch.
결리다 = to feel stiff/cramped, the natural verb for stiff shoulders
운동하고 나서 다리에 파스 붙였어요.
After working out I put a patch on my leg.
-고 나서 = after doing
파스 냄새가 좀 나지만 시원해요.
The patch smells a bit but it feels soothing.
시원하다 here = a cooling, relieving sensation
nuance: 파스 is the everyday word for the medicated patches Koreans slap on sore muscles, stiff necks, and tired legs; it comes from a loanword and has no -제 suffix. The verb is 붙이다 (stick on), and people often mention the strong menthol 냄새 (smell). Casual and very common in daily life.
mistakes: Saying 파스 바르다 — a patch is stuck on (붙이다); only the cream/spray type uses 바르다/뿌리다
Treating 파스 as a pill; it's external only

usage: 장 is the counter for flat/sheet items
examples: 손을 베어서 반창고 붙였어요.
I cut my hand so I put on a band-aid.
(손을) 베다 = to cut oneself
반창고 한 장만 주실 수 있어요?
Could you give me just one band-aid?
Polite request with -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요?
물집 잡혔는데 반창고 붙이는 게 나아요.
I got a blister, so it's better to put on a band-aid.
물집(이) 잡히다 = to get a blister
nuance: 반창고 is the standard word for an adhesive bandage; many Koreans also say the brand name 대일밴드 or just 밴드. The verb is 붙이다, and you count them with 장. Completely neutral, used by everyone.
mistakes: Confusing 반창고 (small adhesive strip) with 붕대 (a roll of gauze bandage)
Using 바르다 instead of 붙이다 — band-aids are stuck on

usage: I wrapped a bandage around my ankle
Particle 에 marks the body part
examples: 발목을 삐어서 붕대로 감았어요.
I sprained my ankle so I wrapped it with a bandage.
발목을 삐다 = to sprain one's ankle
상처가 커서 붕대로 감아야 해요.
The wound is big so it has to be wrapped with a bandage.
Use 붕대 (not 반창고) for larger areas
붕대를 너무 꽉 감지 마세요.
Don't wrap the bandage too tightly.
꽉 = tightly; -지 마세요 = don't
nuance: 붕대 is the rolled gauze bandage you wind around a sprain or larger wound, and the verb is 감다 (wrap), not 붙이다. Use it for ankles, wrists, and big cuts, whereas 반창고 is for small everyday nicks. Neutral register.
mistakes: Using 붕대 붙이다 — a bandage is wrapped (감다), not stuck on
Confusing 붕대 with 반창고; 붕대 is the long roll, 반창고 is the small strip

usage: 바르다 for putting it on the skin
I cleaned the wound with antiseptic
examples: 상처에 소독약 먼저 바르고 연고 바르세요.
Put antiseptic on the wound first, then apply ointment.
Standard wound-care order
넘어진 데를 소독약으로 깨끗이 닦았어요.
I cleaned the spot where I fell with antiseptic.
깨끗이 = cleanly; 데 = spot
소독약 바르니까 좀 따가워요.
It stings a bit when I put on the antiseptic.
따갑다 = to sting; -(으)니까 shows cause
nuance: 소독약 is the everyday term for wound antiseptics like 포비돈(povidone) or 과산화수소(hydrogen peroxide); pharmacists know it instantly. You 바르다 or 닦다 it onto a cut, and people often comment that it 따가워요 (stings). Neutral, practical vocabulary for any home first-aid kit.
mistakes: Saying 소독약 먹다 — antiseptic is for external use, never swallowed
Confusing 소독약 (for wounds) with 소독제 (general disinfectant for surfaces/hands)

usage: Asking at a pharmacy or at home
examples: 체온계로 열을 재 보니까 38.5도였어요.
When I measured my fever with a thermometer, it was 38.5 degrees.
열을 재다 = to take one's temperature
집에 체온계가 없어서 약국에서 샀어요.
I didn't have a thermometer at home so I bought one at the pharmacy.
약국 sells them too
아기 체온계는 귀에 대는 게 편해요.
For a baby, the ear thermometer is convenient.
귀에 대다 = to put against the ear
nuance: 체온계 is specifically the device for measuring body temperature, and the verb pairing is 열을 재다 (take temperature). Since COVID, digital and 귀 (ear) types are everywhere, and you can buy one at any 약국. Neutral register.
mistakes: Confusing 체온계 (body temperature) with 온도계 (general thermometer for air/water)
Using 보다 instead of 재다 — you 재다 (measure) temperature, not 보다

usage: Please give me some stomach medicine
My stomach was burning so I took stomach medicine
속이 쓰리다 = to have a burning/sour stomach
stomach medicine on an empty stomach
examples: 요즘 속이 자주 쓰려서 위장약 먹고 있어요.
These days my stomach often burns, so I'm taking stomach medicine.
Common chronic complaint phrasing
빈속에 커피 마시면 속이 안 좋아서 위장약 챙겨요.
Coffee on an empty stomach upsets my stomach, so I keep stomach medicine handy.
속이 안 좋다 = to feel queasy/upset
술 마시기 전에 위장약 먹는 사람도 있어요.
Some people take stomach medicine before drinking.
Reflects real Korean drinking culture
nuance: 위장약 is the broad term for stomach/gut medicine covering acid, burning (속쓰림), and gastritis, and is distinct from 소화제, which is just for digestion after overeating. Pharmacists will ask your symptom (속쓰림, 더부룩함, 통증) before choosing. Neutral, very practical for adults in Korea.
mistakes: Using 위장약 and 소화제 interchangeably — 위장약 treats acid/pain, 소화제 helps digestion
Saying 위약 — the correct word is 위장약

usage: Common to ask for liquid or powder instead
알 is the counter for round small things
examples: 저는 알약을 잘 못 삼켜요. 물약으로 주세요.
I can't swallow pills well. Please give me the liquid form.
물약 = liquid medicine; useful alternative request
이 알약은 하루에 두 알씩 드세요.
Take two of these tablets a day.
두 알씩 = two pills each (time); 씩 = per/each
알약이 너무 커서 반으로 잘라 먹었어요.
The pill was too big so I cut it in half and took it.
반으로 자르다 = to cut in half
nuance: 알약 is the everyday word for a solid pill or tablet, contrasted with 가루약 (powder) and 물약 (liquid). Counting uses 알, and the verbs are 먹다 or, more precisely, 삼키다 (swallow). If swallowing is hard, it's normal to ask the pharmacist for 물약 or 가루약. Neutral register.
mistakes: Confusing the counter: it's 한 알, not 한 개, for pills
Saying 약알 — the correct order is 알약
